findings.element: 2026 Consensus Forecast Table — 'KEY VIEW' column
findings.detail: The 'Key View' column text is visibly cut off for every institution row (e.g., Goldman Sachs shows 'fading tariff drag growth, below-c', BCA Research shows 'Two-stage 2026: tech broad selloff HQ as labo oil, tech capex t'). The column container is too narrow to display the full commentary, making this column effectively unreadable in a board context.

findings.element: Sector tiles — commentary bullet points
findings.detail: The bullet-point commentary text within each sector tile (Passenger Airlines, Hotels & Accommodations, Restaurants & Food Svcs, etc.) is rendered at an extremely small font size — estimated 6–7px — making it illegible without zooming in. This would be unreadable in a printed board deck.

findings.element: Sector tiles — 'Drivers / CN' commentary text
findings.detail: Within multiple sector tiles (e.g., E-Commerce, Pharmaceuticals/GLP-1, Commercial RE/Office), the commentary lines are truncated mid-sentence with no ellipsis or indication of continuation, cutting off key context visible to the CEO audience.

findings.element: 'So what' commentary — Exhibit 02 (Consensus Indicators chart)
findings.detail: The 'So what' note reads: 'Consensus is bracketing a soft-landing path with growing tail risk — the dispersion between forecasters is wider than at any point since 2022.' This is only one sentence, violating the minimum of 2 sentences required for fc-note commentary.

findings.element: 'So what' commentary — Exhibit 01 (Quarterly GDP chart)
findings.detail: The 'So what' note reads: 'The Q4 deceleration into +1.4% is the cleanest run-rate signal — 2026 enters with weaker momentum than the full-year +2.2% suggests.' This is only one sentence, violating the minimum of 2 sentences required.

findings.element: 'So what' commentary — 2026 Consensus Forecast Table
findings.detail: The 'So what' note reads: 'Stanford SIEPR sits at the bearish end (~40% recession odds); Goldman is the clearest soft-landing voice. The dispersion is the headline — not the midpoint.' This is only 2 sentences and borderline acceptable, but the first sentence contains hedging language ('clearest soft-landing voice') that may conflict with forbidden vocabulary rules.

findings.element: Week 44 top-of-tab fc-note commentary block
findings.detail: The top-level commentary paragraph (beginning 'Real GDP growth of 2.0% annualized…') appears to sit between the navigation header and the first chart section rather than clearly preceding the first chart as a distinct labeled fc-note block. The visual separation is ambiguous and could be mistaken for a subtitle rather than the required preceding commentary.

findings.element: Sector tiles grid — bottom row (Federal Government, Freight & Logistics)
findings.detail: The bottom row of sector tiles contains only 2 tiles (Federal Government and Freight & Logistics) while all other rows contain 5 tiles, creating a visibly unbalanced and incomplete-looking grid layout that appears broken rather than intentional.

findings.element: Source lines — all exhibits and bottom of page
findings.detail: Source attribution text at the bottom of charts and the full-page source line is rendered at approximately 5–6px, well below any legible threshold for print or screen presentation at board level.

findings.element: Sector tiles — vertical spacing between tile rows
findings.detail: The vertical gap between the first row of sector tiles and the second row appears tighter than the gap between the second and third rows, creating inconsistent rhythm across the sector grid panel.

findings.element: Sector panel mini-charts and commentary text
findings.detail: The commentary text beneath each sector panel (e.g., State/Local Govt, Federal Govt, Banking, etc.) is rendered at an extremely small font size — estimated 6–7px — making it unreadable at normal viewing scale in a board deck context.

findings.element: Sector panel bar-chart axis labels and GDP share figures
findings.detail: Year labels (22, 23, 24, 25) and the small GDP-share percentage rows inside each sector tile are rendered below readable threshold (~6px), making them illegible without zooming.

findings.element: Bottom data-source footnote line
findings.detail: The full-width footnote at the very bottom of the dashboard ('Sources: BEA GDP PCE; BLS CPI, Jobs, Wages, Unemployment…') is rendered at approximately 5–6px and is completely illegible.

findings.element: Annual sector-contribution table — cell values and trend column
findings.detail: The numeric cells and 'TREND' column labels in the bottom summary table ('Real GDP held 2.0% in 2025…') are very small and low-contrast against the white background, making them difficult to read in a board presentation.

findings.element: GDP Commentary box — body text
findings.detail: The commentary paragraph appears to be clipped on the right edge on smaller viewports; the last few words of each sentence risk being cut off depending on render width.

findings.element: GDP Commentary — 2025 Growth & 2026 Outlook (EX 1)
findings.detail: The commentary block contains hedging filler language ('makes that trajectory difficult to sustain', 'providing false comfort') and runs to approximately 5–6 sentences, exceeding the 2–4 sentence maximum.

findings.element: EX 2 commentary — 'Real GDP held 2.0% in 2025'
findings.detail: The EX 2 label and its title text appear directly above the table, which is correct, but the EX 1 GDP Commentary box is positioned above the KPI tiles rather than immediately above the first chart panel — the sector grid charts begin before the commentary is fully separated from the KPI row.

findings.element: Sector panel grid — bottom two rows (Cruise Lines, Travel Agencies)
findings.detail: The last row contains only 2 panels (Cruise Lines, Travel Agencies) while all other rows have 5–6 panels, leaving a large blank area to the right. This creates a visually unbalanced layout that would be noticeable in a board deck.

findings.element: Sector panel rows — vertical gap between rows
findings.detail: The vertical spacing between some sector panel rows appears inconsistent — notably the gap before the E-Commerce/Grocery Retail row appears slightly larger than gaps between other rows, suggesting a layout drift.

findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.element: Unemployment tab
findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.element: TOP SECTOR metric tile (KPI card row)
findings.detail: The 'Top Sector' KPI tile displays 'Investmen t Banking' with a visible line break mid-word, truncating/wrapping the label in a way that is unprofessional for a board-level deck.

findings.element: Source footnotes beneath EX 3 and EX 5 (sector table)
findings.detail: Source lines and methodology footnotes are rendered at an extremely small font size (appears ~6–7px), making them effectively unreadable at normal viewing scale. While footnotes are secondary, they must still be legible per style guide standards.

findings.element: EX 4 — Sector wage growth bar chart, Y-axis sector labels
findings.detail: Sector name labels on the left Y-axis of the horizontal bar chart are very small and difficult to read at dashboard viewing size, risking illegibility in a board presentation context.

findings.element: EX 4 — Sector wage growth bar chart, X-axis
findings.detail: The X-axis tick labels on the horizontal bar chart appear compressed and potentially overlapping at the scale rendered, reducing readability.

findings.element: EX 2 — Wage growth decelerated chart, 'So what' callout
findings.detail: The 'So what' analytical commentary line appears below the EX 2 chart rather than above it, preceding the chart. Style guide §1 requires the fc-note/commentary to precede (appear above) the first chart on the tab.

findings.element: EX 2 — 'So what' commentary callout below chart
findings.detail: The 'So what' callout reads: 'A thinning real-wage cushion plus 3.6% savings rate means consumer spending is increasingly drawn from buffers — vulnerable to any renewed inflation impulse.' This is a single sentence, falling below the minimum 2-sentence requirement for commentary blocks.

findings.element: EX 3 — Real wages turned positive chart
findings.detail: The EX 3 line chart has a legend box visible but it appears very small and low-contrast at the rendered size, making it difficult to confirm the nominal vs. real series mapping is clearly distinguishable for a board audience.

findings.element: Stickiest Category metric tile
findings.detail: The category label 'Transportation Svcs' appears to overflow its tile container, with text wrapping awkwardly and potentially clipping at the tile boundary.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 — Headline CPI line chart axis labels and annotations
findings.detail: The x-axis date labels and several inline data annotations (e.g., values along the Headline CPI and Core CPI lines) are rendered at a very small font size and are difficult to read at dashboard viewing scale, particularly the older date labels on the left side of the chart.

findings.element: Exhibit 9 — Energy and transport horizontal bar chart, category labels and bar annotations
findings.detail: Category labels on the y-axis and percentage annotations on the bars are extremely small and low-contrast against the background, making them illegible at normal viewing distance for a board-level audience.

findings.element: Exhibit 5 — Annual CPI bar chart, x-axis year labels
findings.detail: The x-axis year labels spanning from ~1990 to 2025 are rendered at a very small size and are difficult to read, with individual years indistinguishable at board presentation scale.

findings.element: Vertical spacing between Exhibit 6 / Exhibit 8 panel group and Exhibit 7 panel below
findings.detail: There is a noticeably large vertical gap between the Goods inflation / Category-level annual rates row (Exhibits 6 & 8) and the Trimmed-mean and median CPI chart (Exhibit 7) below it, significantly more whitespace than between other panel rows on the same tab.

findings.element: Exhibit 7 — Trimmed-mean and median CPI line chart, legend and axis labels
findings.detail: The legend entries and x-axis date labels in the Trimmed-mean/Median CPI chart are rendered at a very small font size, making the series labels and time axis difficult to distinguish at board-level viewing distance.

findings.element: Exhibit 6 — Goods inflation horizontal bar chart, category and value labels
findings.detail: Category labels on the y-axis and bar value annotations are very small and hard to read, particularly for the lower categories (e.g., 'Used Cars & Trucks', 'Apparel').

findings.element: Exhibit 7 — Trimmed-mean and median CPI line chart, data point annotations
findings.detail: Several inline value annotations on the line chart appear to overlap each other in the right-hand portion of the chart where the lines converge, making individual values unreadable.

findings.element: Exhibit 8 — Category-level annual rates table, 'Food at Home' 2024 column
findings.detail: The 2024 value for 'Food at Home' displays as '---' or a placeholder rather than an actual numeric value, suggesting missing or unformatted data in a board-facing table.

findings.element: Footer source lines at bottom of page
findings.detail: The data source attribution text at the very bottom of the dashboard is rendered at an extremely small font size, well below readable threshold even for fine print in a board document.

findings.detail: The commentary block contains hedging language ('cannot declare victory', 'effectively on hold but cannot credibly pivot') and runs to what appears to be 4+ dense sentences that may exceed the style guide's sentence-count ceiling and include filler qualifiers.

findings.detail: The x-axis year labels and the legend text ('Single-family / Multi-family') are extremely small and difficult to read at dashboard viewing scale, falling below the minimum legible body text size for a board-level presentation.

findings.element: Exhibit EX 6 — Affordability Index / Months Supply dual-panel chart (axis labels)
findings.detail: Both the top and bottom panel axis tick labels and the legend text are rendered at a very small font size, making them illegible without zooming in. This is particularly problematic for a CEO/board audience.

findings.element: Footer source line (bottom of page)
findings.detail: The full-page source attribution line at the very bottom of the dashboard is rendered in extremely small, low-contrast gray text that is effectively illegible at normal viewing size.

findings.element: EX 3 — Home Prices chart (x-axis year labels)
findings.detail: The x-axis year labels on the Case-Shiller national home price index chart are very small and densely packed, making individual years difficult to distinguish at board presentation resolution.

findings.element: EX 5 — Housing Starts bar chart (x-axis)
findings.detail: The x-axis year labels appear to be densely packed and potentially overlapping given the number of years displayed (1990–2025) in the available chart width, risking illegibility in a board deck context.

findings.element: EX 2 — 'So what' commentary below Mortgage Rate chart
findings.detail: The 'So what' sentence reads: 'Rates need to break below ~5.5% to unlock the lock-in cohort — until then, transaction volume stays compressed and price discovery is thin.' This is a single sentence, falling below the style guide minimum of 2 sentences for per-chart commentary.

findings.element: EX 3 — 'So what' commentary below Home Prices chart
findings.detail: The 'So what' line appears to be a single sentence ('Affordability deterioration has compounded — the price-to-income gap is the structural drag on transaction volume'), which is below the 2-sentence minimum required by the style guide.

findings.element: EX 4 — 'So what' commentary below Mortgage Rate Gap chart
findings.detail: The 'So what' note appears to be a single sentence, falling below the style guide minimum of 2 sentences for per-chart commentary.

findings.element: EX 7 — Metro table 'TREND' column sparkline/indicator labels
findings.detail: The trend indicator labels ('↑ Fading', '↑ Rising') in the TREND column are small and the directional arrows may be difficult to distinguish at reduced resolution in a printed board deck.

findings.element: EX 5 and EX 6 panel pair vs. EX 3 and EX 4 panel pair
findings.detail: The vertical spacing between the bottom of the EX 5/EX 6 panel row and the EX 7 table below appears visibly tighter than the spacing between the EX 2 panel and the EX 3/EX 4 panel row above, creating inconsistent inter-panel rhythm.

findings.element: Footer data source line (bottom of dashboard)
findings.detail: The footer citation text listing all data sources is rendered at an extremely small font size (appears to be ~6–7px), making it effectively unreadable at normal viewing distance. This would be called out in a board-level review.

findings.element: Chart R7 — Annual WTI axis labels and recession shading labels
findings.detail: X-axis year labels and the inline 'Recession year' legend text in the bottom-left historical oil shock chart are too small to read clearly at dashboard resolution, particularly the early-decade year markers.

findings.element: Oil Supply Shock Tracker (Section 2, R6) — sub-metric annotations
findings.detail: The small annotation text beneath the WTI/Brent latest price tiles (e.g., session count, spread figures) and the crisis range labels are rendered at a very small size, making them illegible without zooming in.

findings.element: Full Oil Impact Chain tracker (Section 2, R8) — node detail rows
findings.detail: The descriptive body text within each phase node (e.g., 'Pump prices spike', BLS/CPI references, margin figures) is rendered at approximately 7–8px, well below a readable threshold for a CEO-level board deck.

findings.element: Metric tiles — top KPI bar (e.g., 'GASBUDGET CURRENT', 'NEER/BRENT')
findings.detail: Several KPI tile labels in the top summary bar appear to have their header label text compressed or partially cut off (e.g., 'GASBUDGET CURRENT' runs together without spacing), suggesting container width is insufficient for the label copy.

findings.element: Section 4 — Recession Signal History commentary block
findings.detail: The 'fc-note' commentary paragraph for Section 4 appears to sit between the section header and the charts, which is correct in principle, but the Oil Commentary block at the very top (Section 1) is followed immediately by metric tiles rather than the first chart — the commentary block for the tab overall precedes the tiles, which may be compliant, but Section 4's note wraps tightly against the chart below with no clear visual separation, risking it being read as a chart caption rather than a preceding note.

findings.element: Section 4 — Recession Signal History commentary
findings.detail: The commentary contains hedging language ('causality is debated', 'Worth monitoring if') which is likely on the forbidden vocabulary list. The note also runs to what appears to be a single long run-on sentence rather than 2–4 discrete sentences as required.

findings.element: Section 3 — Sector Impact table vs. surrounding sections
findings.detail: The vertical padding between the Section 3 header rule and the table content appears noticeably tighter than the equivalent spacing in Sections 1, 2, and 4, creating an inconsistent rhythm across panels.

findings.element: R7 — Historical oil shocks line chart (bottom left)
findings.detail: The chart plots at least two series (WTI line and recession shading bands) but the inline legend is extremely small and the color key for the gold/orange line versus the recession shading is not clearly labeled at readable size, making series identification difficult for a board audience.
